title: the live page: the house match on the public site, and join to play
summary: v0.6.0-poc put the game in the player's tab. v0.7.0-poc puts a match on the public page, for anyone, without joining: /live. What it shows is the house match, a Doom game the host runs on its own machine with two robots, and with the players who chose to play in it after being told it is broadcast. A player's own game never reaches the page. A streamer on the host reads the house's spectator and pushes its frames out to the page with a token of its own; the page never connects in, keeps only the last picture in memory and limits its viewers; panic takes it offline. Join and play is the same path as always: ask on the page, join with your own machine, open your console, accept the house's party, press Play. Below, a real poc-doom run, from the robots' match to petersen playing in the broadcast match.

player.title: The players: petersen plays in the match the public page shows
steps: Anyone opens /live on the public page and watches the house match, about two pictures a second, without joining anything.
The host's house offers a party to every player; nothing opens until a player accepts it, and the accept says the match is broadcast.

petersen accepts and plays from her own machine; the page counts one player in the match. When the host closes the house her party closes too, and she must accept again before playing when it reopens.

host.title: The host: a house match, a streamer, and an off switch
steps: mesh host house init and start: the house's server, two robots and its spectator run on the host's own machine, never the control plane, with no credential in the namespace.
mesh host live start: the streamer pushes the spectator's frames out to the page with the stream token; the page keeps only its hash and the last picture.
house close withdraws every offer and closes the parties; panic takes the page offline, and clearing it brings the match back.

features.name: The live page
features.what: /live on the public page: the house match's last picture, about two a second, for anyone; the page keeps it in memory only, limits viewers per address and in total, and takes no input from visitors.
features.why: A match anyone can watch, without a new way into the host's lab.

features.name: The house match
features.what: The host's own Doom game in its namespace house, on its own machine: a server, two robots and a spectator. Open, it offers a party to every player; only the player's accept opens it, and the accept says it is broadcast.
features.why: Only people who chose to be shown are shown; a player's own game never is.
features.command:
mesh host house init
mesh host house start
mesh host house open

features.name: The streamer
features.what: On the host, outbound only: it reads the house's spectator and pushes its frames to the page with its own token (the page keeps its SHA-256); panic, or stopping it, tells the page offline.
features.why: The public server holds no credential of the cluster and never connects in.
features.command:
page-server.sh stream-token --ssh "..."
mesh host live start --url https://<the public page>

features.name: Join and play
features.what: The live page's steps: ask on the public page, join with your own machine, open edge-mesh console, Join the house match (broadcast), then Play.
features.why: Playing in the broadcast match is the same consented path as any other game.
features.command:
edge-mesh party accept house
edge-mesh console   # Play
